identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log

scan.summary: This is a maintenance and safety record documenting daily pre-shift inspections of a Toyota propane forklift (unit FL-2) at the Portland warehouse for September 2026. It shows inspection results against 12 checklist items required by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), with equipment hours logged and operator initials recorded for each inspection.
scan.freshness_note: This log is current as of 18 September 2026, three days before today (29 September 2026). The supervisor review line is blank and undated, which is a gap.

gaps.title: Missing inspections for September 3-6
gaps.description: The hour meter shows the truck ran on 5-6 September (hours increased from 4,819 at Sep 2 to 4,834 at Sep 7), but no inspections are documented for Sep 3, 4, 5, or 6. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) requires examination before the truck is placed in service each shift.
gaps.fix: Conduct and document inspections for the missing dates, or if the truck did not run those days, correct the hour meter record. If inspections cannot be reconstructed, document why and ensure no gaps remain going forward.
gaps.locator: Page 2, note states 'The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.'
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: No supervisor review signature or date
gaps.description: The log form has a line for 'Supervisor review' with blanks for signature and date, but both are left blank and unsigned. This undermines accountability and verification of the log's completeness.
gaps.fix: Have a supervisor sign and date the log to certify that they have reviewed the inspections and that all required entries have been completed.
gaps.citation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) (requires documented examination); Oregon Administrative Rules OAR 437-004-1178(q)(7) (likely mirrors federal standard)

gaps.title: Defect not resolved—horn not working on September 9
gaps.description: On 9 September, the horn was marked with an X (defect) with the note 'Horn not working'. The log shows the truck continued to be used on subsequent days, but there is no record of when the horn was repaired or whether a work order was issued. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) states the truck shall not be placed in service if examination shows a condition adversely affecting safety.
gaps.fix: Document the corrective action taken: when the horn was repaired, by whom, and verification that it was tested and working before the truck returned to service. If it was repaired before the next inspection (Sep 10), document that. If not, explain why the truck was used after the defect was noted.
gaps.locator: Page 1, Sep 9 row, Horn column marked X with note 'Horn not working'

conditions.title: Examination before each shift
conditions.evidence_expected: Pre-shift inspection log showing date, time or shift, all 12 checklist items reviewed (tires, forks, mast, horn, lights, seatbelt, brakes, steering, propane tank, fire extinguisher, data plate, overhead guard), operator signature or initials, and notes on any defects found.

conditions.title: No defective truck in service
conditions.evidence_expected: Log entry showing when defects are found, when they are reported to maintenance, when repairs are completed, and verification that the truck was not used until the defect was corrected. For Sep 9 horn defect, repair completion record.

conditions.title: Operator training and certification
conditions.evidence_expected: Operator certification records for M. Chen and J. Rivera showing training date, evaluation date, and re-evaluation due date. Log shows M. Chen certified 2024-03-11 (evaluation due 2027-03-11) and J. Rivera certified 2025-06-02 (evaluation due 2028-06-02).

expected_missing.title: Monthly or annual maintenance inspection record
expected_missing.why: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(8) implies more detailed maintenance inspections beyond daily pre-shift checks; detailed inspection records would typically accompany a pre-shift log.

expected_missing.title: Documentation of training and re-evaluation for forklift operators
expected_missing.why: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(l) requires formal training records, evaluation records, and certificates of training; these would normally be filed separately from the operational log.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

scan.confidence_notes: I am confident in identifying the document kind (record), the subject matter (workplace safety), the applicable rule (OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7)), and the three substantive gaps: missing inspections for Sep 3-6, missing supervisor sign-off, and unresolved horn defect. The operator certification information is clearly stated and I have verified the 3-year re-evaluation rule under 1910.178(l)(4) via web search. I am less confident in assessing whether the missing inspections on Sep 12-13 are also violations without knowing the company's actual operational schedule, but the document itself and the meter reading note establish that Sep 3-6 inspections were missing despite equipment use. The log does not indicate which jurisdiction's rules apply beyond the OSHA citation, but OSHA is federal and Oregon likely mirrors it in OAR 437-004-1178.
